\begin{align*}&\text{1. Variables: } y,\ x,\ t \text{ with } x^2+y^2=25,\ y=\sqrt{25-x^2}\\&\text{2. Chain rule: } \frac{dy}{dt}=\frac{dy}{dx}\times\frac{dx}{dt}\\&\text{3. Differentiate and substitute:}\\\frac{dy}{dt}&=-\frac{x}{\sqrt{25-x^2}}\times0.4\\&=-\frac{0.4x}{y}\\&\text{4. Evaluate: at } x=3,\ y=\sqrt{25-9}=4\\\frac{dy}{dt}&=-\frac{0.4(3)}{4}\\&=-0.3\\&\text{The top slides down at } 0.3\text{ m/s.}\end{align*}

[Pedagogy audit v2 · Applied automatically · Extension] After the circle question, students should see that dA/dr = 2πr is the circumference and dV/dr = 4πr² is the surface area. Then dV/dt = (surface area) × dr/dt in the balloon question.
Proposed question: A circle of area $A$ and a sphere of surface area $S$ and volume $V$ each have radius $r$.
a) Find $\dfrac{dA}{dr}$ and compare it with the circumference of the circle.
b) Find $\dfrac{dV}{dr}$ and write it in terms of $S$.
c) Hence show that $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=S\dfrac{dr}{dt}$.
d) The radius of a sphere is increasing at $0.3\text{ cm/s}$ at the instant its surface area is $200\text{ cm}^2$. Find the rate at which its volume is increasing at this instant.
Answers: a) $\dfrac{dA}{dr}=2\pi r$, which is the circumference.; b) $\dfrac{dV}{dr}=4\pi r^2=S$.; c) $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=\dfrac{dV}{dr}\times\dfrac{dr}{dt}=S\dfrac{dr}{dt}$.; d) $60\text{ cm}^3/\text{s}$.

entries.description:
2020 HSC Extension 1 Band 4
The quantities P, Q and R are connected by the related rates:
\frac{dR}{dt}=-k^2
\frac{dP}{dt}=-l^2\times\frac{dR}{dt}
\frac{dP}{dt}=m^2\times\frac{dQ}{dt}
where k, l and m are non-zero constants.
Which of the following statements is true?
A. P is increasing and Q is increasing
B. P is increasing and Q is decreasing
C. P is decreasing and Q is increasing
D. P is decreasing and Q is decreasing
entries.expectedAnswer: A. P is increasing and Q is increasing
entries.presentation: Black question text; three displayed related-rate equations stacked with aligned equals signs. Four options appear vertically in A–D order. The year/examination/band source identity is bold.

entries.description:
Given: \frac{dR}{dt}=-k^2<0 (since k^2>0)
\frac{dP}{dt}=-l^2\times\frac{dR}{dt}=-l^2\times(-k^2)=l^2k^2>0
\frac{dP}{dt}=m^2\times\frac{dQ}{dt}, so \frac{dQ}{dt}=\frac{\frac{dP}{dt}}{m^2}=\frac{l^2k^2}{m^2}>0
Therefore P is increasing and Q is increasing.
A
entries.presentation: Supplied blue worked answer at the right below the question equations; retain as answer-only content.

In triangle APG: r² = AG² + PG²

dr/dt = (dr/du) × (du/dt)

du/dt = 360 km/h

entries.description:
In realistic models of growth and decay, the change is proportional to the difference of the current value to some constant value, P.
Larger difference means faster change.

If Q = P + Ae^{kt}, dQ/dt = kAe^{kt}
= k(P + Ae^{kt} − P)
= k(Q − P).
An underbrace beneath P + A identifies the initial quantity, with the annotation “initial quantity” and “t = 0”.

presentation.arrangement: Defining expression on the left; three-line derivative working on the right, aligned at equals signs.
presentation.annotation: Keep the underbrace and its initial-quantity annotation attached to P + A.

entries.description: Four side-by-side cases, in source order: k < 0, A > 0; k < 0, A < 0; k > 0, A > 0; k > 0, A < 0.

presentation.arrangement: One horizontal row of four graphs, each with its two sign conditions above it.

entries.description: Case k < 0, A > 0. Axes Q vertically and t horizontally, with arrowheads. A blue decreasing, concave-up curve begins at Q = P + A on the vertical axis and approaches the horizontal blue dotted asymptote Q = P from above. Vertical-axis labels P + A and P; curve has a rightward arrow.

Case k < 0, A < 0. Axes Q vertically and t horizontally, with arrowheads. A blue increasing, concave-down curve begins at Q = P + A on the vertical axis and approaches the horizontal blue dotted asymptote Q = P from below. Vertical-axis labels P and P + A; curve has a rightward arrow.

Case k > 0, A > 0. Axes Q vertically and t horizontally, with arrowheads. A blue increasing, concave-up curve starts at the vertical-axis label P + A and rises steeply, ending with an arrow. No asymptote is drawn.

Case k > 0, A < 0. Axes Q vertically and t horizontally, with arrowheads. A blue decreasing, concave-down curve starts at the vertical-axis label P + A and reaches the horizontal axis. No asymptote is drawn.

We will focus on cases where k < 0.
When k < 0, the quantity Q approaches a limiting value P as t → ∞.
This limiting value P can represent:
• ambient temperature; hot objects cool towards room temperature.
• carrying capacity; populations stabilise at the maximum an environment can support.

presentation.arrangement: Concluding explanation beneath the four graphs, followed by two bullet points.

entries.description:
Finding the value of k.
Modified growth and decay problems usually involve finding the value of k.
If dQ/dt = k(Q − P), then Q = P + Ae^(kt).
1. Write Q = P + Ae^(kt). Remember that P is the limiting value and A + P is the initial value.
2. Substitute in given values and solve for k. Leave in exact form.
3. Rewrite equation with P, A and k.
4. Solve for what the question asks for.
In questions where you need to find the derivative or solve for t, write k instead of its exact value to avoid writing a complex logarithm every line.

entries.description: A saucepan of water is brought nearly to the boil then removed from the heat. The temperature reaches 95°C and room temperature is a constant 25°C. If the water has lost 25% of its excess heat after 2.5 minutes, find how long it will take for it to cool down to 30°C.
entries.presentation: Black question text above a large open working region. Best-fit skill: Newton’s law of cooling using exponential decay.

entries.description:
Using T = 25 + Ae^{-kt}:
t = 0: 95 = 25 + A
so A = 70
Excess heat initially = 95 − 25 = 70°C
After 2.5 minutes, lost 25% of excess heat means 75% remains
Remaining excess heat = 0.75 × 70 = 52.5°C
So T = 25 + 52.5 = 77.5°C
t = 2.5: 77.5 = 25 + 70e^{-2.5k}
52.5 = 70e^{-2.5k}
e^{-2.5k} = 3/4
k = (1/2.5) ln(4/3) = (2/5) ln(4/3)
For T = 30°C:
30 = 25 + 70e^{-kt}
5 = 70e^{-kt}
e^{-kt} = 1/14
t = ln(1/14)/(−k) = 16 minutes
entries.presentation: Blue supplied answer, arranged as successive right-aligned lines. Preserve explanatory text and equation order; keep outside the student prompt.
